accepted.question_text: Is the maximal abelian extension Qab of the rational numbers Q an ample field, where a field K is called ample when every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points, equivalently when K satisfies the other equivalent conditions listed in Proposition 2.1?
accepted.context_brief: Ampleness of the maximal abelian extension of Q

evidence.quote: An ample field is a field K that satisfies the equivalent conditions (1)-(4).
Question I. Is Qab ample?

accepted.question_text: Is the maximal solvable Galois extension Qsolv of Q an ample field?
accepted.context_brief: Ampleness of the maximal solvable extension of Q

evidence.quote: It is interesting to note that it is even unknown whether the bigger field Qsolv, the maximal solvable Galois extension of Q, is ample.

accepted.question_text: Is the maximal solvable Galois extension Qsolv of Q pseudo algebraically closed, meaning that every absolutely irreducible Q-variety has a Qsolv-rational point? Equivalently, does every absolutely irreducible Q-variety admit a solvable rational point?

evidence.quote: Here, a field K is called pseudo algebraically closed (PAC, see [FJ08]) if every absolutely irreducible K-variety has a K-rational point.

Even worse, while Frey proved that Qab is not PAC, [FJ08, Corollary 11.5.7], it is a long-standing open question whether Qsolv is PAC, equivalently, whether every absolutely irreducible Q-variety admits a solvable rational point.

accepted.question_text: Fix a finite set S of places of Q, and let Qtot,S be the maximal extension of Q in which every place in S is totally split. Is the field Qtot,S intersected with Qsolv pseudo S-closed (PSC), where a subfield K of Qtot,S is PSC if every smooth Q-variety that has a point over Qp for each p in S (with Q_infinity = R) has a K-rational point?
accepted.context_brief: Whether Qtot,S intersect Qsolv is PSC

evidence.quote: A typical example of an ample field that does not fall into any of these categories is the field of totally S-adic numbers Qtot,S, S a finite set of places of Q - the maximal extension of Q in which each place in S is totally split.

An example of such fields are the PSC fields: If S is a finite set of places of Q, then a field K <= Qtot,S is called PSC if every smooth Q-variety that has a point over Qp for each p in S (with Qinfty = R) has a K-rational point.
This fact plays an important role in the study of potential modularity of Galois representations, which motivated Taylor to ask in [Tay04] whether also Qtot,S intersect Qsolv is PSC.

accepted.question_text: For every non-zero abelian variety A defined over Q, is the Mordell-Weil rank of A over Qab infinite; that is, does rank(A(Qab)) = infinity hold for every such A?
accepted.context_brief: Ranks of abelian varieties over Qab

evidence.quote: Question 3.2 (Frey-Jarden). Is rank(A(Qab)) = infinity for every non-zero abelian variety A over Q?

accepted.question_text: If K is an infinite field whose absolute Galois group GK is prosolvable, must K be ample?

evidence.quote: Question II. Is every infinite field K with prosolvable absolute Galois group GK ample?

accepted.question_text: If K is an infinite field whose absolute Galois group GK is finitely generated as a topological group, must K be ample?

evidence.quote: The following question occurs as a conjecture in [JK10]:
Question III. Is every infinite field K with finitely generated absolute Galois group GK ample?

accepted.question_text: Let K/Q be an algebraic extension whose absolute Galois group GK is finitely generated, and let A be a non-zero abelian variety over K. Must the Mordell-Weil rank rank(A(K)) be infinite?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1 (Larsen). Let K/Q be an algebraic extension with GK finitely generated, and let A be a non-zero abelian variety over K. Then rank(A(K)) = infinity.

accepted.question_text: What is the precise relationship among ample fields, virtually ample fields, and weakly ample fields? In particular, if a field K is called virtually ample when some finite extension of K is ample, and weakly ample when every K-curve C becomes infinite over some finite extension L/K, must every weakly ample field be virtually ample, and must every virtually ample field already be ample?
accepted.context_brief: Ample versus virtually ample versus weakly ample

evidence.quote: A field K is virtually ample if some finite extension of K is ample. Exchanging quantifiers in this definition we get a weaker condition: A field K is called weakly ample if for every K-curve C there exists a finite extension L of K such that C(L) is infinite.
Question IV. What is the relation between ample, virtually ample, and weakly ample fields? Is every weakly ample field virtually ample? Is every virtually ample field ample?

accepted.question_text: Is every radically closed field ample, where radically closed means that the multiplicative group K^times of the field is divisible?

evidence.quote: A field K is called radically closed if the multiplicative group Ktimes is divisible.
Question V. Is every radically closed field ample?

accepted.question_text: Is every infinite almost radically closed field ample, where almost radically closed means that for every positive integer n the subgroup of n-th powers has finite index in K^times?

evidence.quote: Call K almost radically closed if for every n the subgroup of n-th powers has finite index in Ktimes.
One could strengthen the above question and ask whether every infinite almost radically closed field is ample.

accepted.question_text: Is every minimal field algebraically closed, where an infinite field K is called minimal when every subset A of K definable by a first-order formula in the language of rings is finite or cofinite?

evidence.quote: An infinite field K is called minimal if every subset A <= K which is definable by a first-order formula in the language of rings is finite or cofinite.
Conjecture 6.1 (Podewski). Every minimal field is algebraically closed.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a non-ample field K such that every finite split embedding problem over K has a regular solution? Equivalently, does there exist a non-ample field K for which the Debes-Deschamps conjecture holds?
accepted.context_brief: Non-ample fields satisfying the Debes-Deschamps conjecture

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1 (D`ebes-Deschamps). Every finite split embedding problem over any field K has a regular solution.
Question VI. Does there exist a non-ample field K for which the conjecture of D`ebes and Deschamps holds?
